messages.subject: zero.add not used in cfa()
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to fit a model with ordinal variables and it seems like, due to a sample size of just N=111, there are quite a lot of empty cells in the correlation tables:

lavaan WARNING: 253 bivariate tables have empty cells

So I read that lavaan has the zero.add option, but when I pass zero.add = c(0.5, 0.5) to cfa(), I still get the same warning. After inspecting the correlation tables, nothing seems to have changed. Also, the robust fit measures are still not calculated, when inspecting them they are set to NA. Is there something I'm missing? Is there a way to set the option so that cfa() accepts it? I also tried it with lavaan() and the defaults used by cfa() but still nothing…

My version is 0.5.23.1097

messages.author: 7f4234085aedc327
messages.subject: Re: zero.add not used in cfa()
parts: Ok, it seems like using zero.add DOES seem to change the fit measures a little bit, but WLSMV simply does not compute the "robust" fit indices. So I assume that using the "scaled" ones is the way to go. Is that correct?

messages.subject: Re: zero.add not used in cfa()
parts: when I pass zero.add = c(0.5, 0.5) to cfa(), I still get the same warning. After inspecting the correlation tables, nothing seems to have changed.

You still get the same warning because your data still have the same property.   Inspecting the data will still show you empty cells because your data do have empty cells.  Plugging in 0.5 will only happen in the background when estimating polychoric correlations.
Also, the robust fit measures are still not calculated, when inspecting them they are set to NA. Is there something I'm missing?

You can find more information in a previous thread about robust CFI, etc.
